specification.outcome: Pi remains visibly responsive while a long tiber_workflow_request evaluates: activity appears promptly, animation continues, and exactly one terminal result replaces progress.

scenarios.name: start and sustain responsive progress
given: request parsing and synchronous setup have completed
dispatch will await work for at least two seconds
then: onUpdate receives a running update before dispatch is invoked and within 100 milliseconds of execute entry
later heartbeats occur no more than once per 1000 milliseconds and no less than once per 2000 milliseconds while still running
an independently scheduled event-loop sentinel executes before the awaited work completes

scenarios.name: complete through one closed progress state machine
given: progress state is idle, running, or terminal
when: success, typed denial, cancellation, timeout, or execution failure occurs
then: only idle-to-running-to-terminal and idle-to-terminal transitions are legal
onUpdate carries running observations only and never percentages or inferred new work
the tool return value alone carries exactly one terminal disposition evaluated, denied, cancelled, timed-out, or failed and all queued progress is suppressed afterward

scenarios.name: propagate cancellation and timeout
given: the caller AbortSignal aborts or the operation time budget expires
when: long-running reviewer or repository work supports cancellation
then: the same signal or a linked timeout signal is passed through dispatch to the operation and its cleanup is awaited
non-abortable work is marked cancelling, receives no further progress, and cannot publish a new consequential effect after cancellation observation
the terminal return is cancelled for caller abort or timed-out for budget expiry

scenarios.name: clean up every race and callback failure
given: dispatch may throw synchronously, onUpdate may throw, abort may race completion, or timer setup may fail
when: the first terminal cause is selected
then: it wins atomically and later causes cannot change the disposition
timers, subscriptions, queued callbacks, and abort listeners are removed
onUpdate failure aborts work and returns failed without recursive progress reporting

acceptanceCriteria: Initial running progress occurs after bounded synchronous parsing/setup but before invoking or awaiting long dispatch, with a 100 millisecond maximum in deterministic-clock tests.
After the initial update, progress is coalesced to one latest non-percentage observation per 1000 milliseconds; a 2000 millisecond watchdog proves continuing work without update flooding.
A setImmediate or equivalent sentinel proves the event loop yields during a two-second fake operation.
Terminal returns have details.disposition evaluated|denied|cancelled|timed-out|failed and safe text; onUpdate never emits terminal authority.
Success, denial, cancellation, timeout, synchronous throw, callback throw, and abort/completion race each leave zero active timers, listeners, subscriptions, or queued updates.
Existing workflow, readiness, role, and effect denial tests remain unchanged and pass.
dependencies: Pi extension execute/onUpdate and AbortSignal contracts
src/adapters/models/pi-readiness-reviewer.ts linked cancellation, heartbeat, and timeout cleanup
specification.architectureImplications: Implement a closed progress state machine in the imperative shell. Progress is bounded UI observation, never authority. Long operations receive linked cancellation and yield the event loop; first terminal cause wins and owns cleanup.
